input.question: Do you know what caused the basement flooding — was it from a problem with your own home's plumbing or drainage system, or did the water come from outside (heavy rain, groundwater, neighbor's property)?

input.value: Returned from work trip, date unknown
Basement and upstairs bathroom (burst supply line)
Burst water supply line under upstairs bathroom sink
Approximately 2 inches of water across entire basement, buckled hardwood floor, drywall soaked to 1 foot height, multiple stored boxes ruined

input.rationale: Damage to the policyholder's own home (basement flooring, drywall, and contents) caused by a burst supply line in the policyholder's own plumbing system is clearly a covered property damage claim.

Extensive water damage affecting structural elements (hardwood flooring, drywall to 1 foot height) and contents across the entire basement indicates probable damage well above $25,000, requiring urgent on-site inspection and mitigation to prevent secondary damage like mold.

input.claim_summary: Sam Patel's basement experienced significant water damage (approximately 2 inches throughout, with buckled hardwood flooring and drywall soaking up to 1 foot height) caused by a burst water supply line under an upstairs bathroom sink. Multiple stored boxes are also damaged. This is a high-severity property damage claim requiring urgent on-site inspection and mitigation.
